claim: Before the streaming fix, `Build::putBlob` could materialize a `BlobSource` into a `String`, producing about 384 MiB peak RSS for a 64 MiB blob upload; testing this risk requires blobs of at least 256 MiB or the `ci/full` scale.
`Build::putBlob` was changed to stream the staged source instead of materializing it in a `String`, resolving the observed CA upload memory blow-up.

Concurrent explicit `SYSTEM CAS GC RUN ca` leaders could permanently orphan unreachable content blobs and part-manifests while preserving safety (`fsck dangling=0`); the leak occurred because an aborted divergent fold advanced generation or cursor state past owner-removal events that were never folded.

The concurrent-leader GC leak arose because `fold()` wrote `gc/gen/<gen>/fold_seal` before the lease-guarded `gc/state` CAS; a divergent `putIfAbsent` caused the losing leader to throw `ABORTED` without advancing state, so the winner's seal was never re-adopted and its owner-removal events were not re-folded.

The concurrent-leader GC fix stores every per-round artifact, including `retired` and `outcomes`, under `gc/gen/<gen>/attempt/<a>/...`, where `<a>` is the folding leader's lease sequence; a lease-guarded adopt CAS publishes `(snap_generation, snap_attempt)`, and readers resolve only that adopted pair.

Unadopted GC attempts are invisible to readers, resume, prune, and `RetireView`, so a deposed leader cannot collide on a final-key seal; unadopted attempt debris is reclaimed by wholesale `gc/gen/<g>/` retention pruning.
A nonzero reclaimable residual in S33 is a real regression of the attempt-scoped generation invariant: concurrent explicit GC leaders left 87 or 84 `_manifests` unreachable while `dangling=0`.
GC per-round fanout grew across create/drop iterations even when no table remained live, violating the D1 registry-removal and dropped-shard-reclaim guarantee.

`cas-gc-dryrun` previews condemned objects in the two-phase graduation pipeline, so its candidates may be in the union of fsck classes `unreachable`, `pending-gc`, and `awaiting-gc`; a bounded `pending-gc` residual at fixpoint is expected rather than a leak.
The `assert_dryrun_subset` oracle must accept `dryrun ⊆ (unreachable ∪ pending-gc ∪ awaiting-gc)` but must fail if a candidate is `reachable`, `dangling`, or absent.

A CA mount could wedge after rapid crash-restart because a GC leader legitimately fenced an expired lease while the renewal thread was blocked by synchronous `refreshViewForBeat` S3 reads, and the non-atomic self-adopt GET-to-CAS window had no retry.

Mount fence recovery treats a `FencedSelf` claim as a typed `MountFencedException`, distinguishes a GC fence of the node's own expired lease from a foreign writer, allocates a fresh `writer_epoch`, and retries the claim in `Store::open`.

Mount lease renewal no longer performs the S3-heavy retired-view refresh; it reads `Store::observedGcRound`, while a dedicated `syncRetiredView` thread advances the view so object-store latency cannot block renewal past the TTL.

The mount fence-recovery implementation still requires live validation under induced S3 latency to prove renewal cadence remains within its period, a live lease does not expire, no spurious `gc_fence_out` occurs, and genuine fence-out recovers as a higher-`writer_epoch` incarnation.

GC cadence should be driven by per-shard journal pressure (event count, body size, or age), not changed-shard count, because one hot shard can accumulate thousands of mutations while still counting as one changed shard.

The GC cadence tradeoff is approximately `A/interval + B·interval`, where `A` is per-fold universe work and `B` is writer amplification from journal growth; the proposed optimal interval scales as `sqrt(U) / r` for blob universe `U` and hottest-shard mutation rate `r`.

The default `gc_fold_threshold` is 1, so a touched active shard is folded and trimmed each round while idle rounds can defer; the proposed production cadence is roughly `gc_interval_sec` 30–60 seconds with journal-pressure triggering.

The CA write path historically spilled an entire part to `disks/ca/cas_scratch` before S3 upload: a 24 GiB part used about 24 GiB scratch and a 100 GiB part used about 93 GiB, so a part larger than local scratch was unwritable despite bounded RSS.

A shared-pool replica independently re-merging and re-spilling the same `OPTIMIZE FINAL` work can consume about 186 GiB local scratch to produce one deduplicated 100 GiB blob; the proposed design is to adopt the leader's already-uploaded content-addressed blob instead.

The idle-GC skip-unchanged mechanism uses `gc_fold_threshold` with default 1 and bounds deferral with `gc_fold_max_defer_rounds`, default 8; `graduationDue` forces a fold before the deferral bound expires.

GC folds remain O(ref-universe) for large deltas: measured duration grew from about 87 ms at 400 parts to 93 seconds at 10,000 tables and 398 seconds at about 100,000 parts, even though correctness held with `dangling=0`.

A 20,000-column wide part can issue about 20,000 object-store operations in one merge, exhausting the ClickHouse container's ephemeral TCP ports and causing `Poco::Net Cannot assign requested address` while the part itself can still commit correctly.
A single INSERT into a 256-partition table can take about 10 seconds because each partition piece performs a separate CAS commit with manifest, ref, and blob round trips.

S22 requires a fault-injecting proxy between the CA disk endpoint and RustFS to inject `503 SlowDown`, `429 Too Many Requests`, latency, and mid-response TCP resets; toxiproxy covers TCP faults but not HTTP status injection.

S27 requires an instrumented S3 proxy that can duplicate root-shard LIST keys, omit a continuation token, or change an otherwise stable list token so `listRootShardTokens` conservative rereads can be exercised.

A converged GC verdict must use the final `fsck_final` after the end-checkpoint fixpoint and must count only reclaimable prefixes `blobs` and `_manifests`; non-reclaimable `other` bookkeeping is tracked separately.

Under recurring content hashes, a resurrected blob incarnation B could replace condemned incarnation A at the same hash key; the exact-token delete guard correctly skipped deleting B, but GC failed to re-condemn B, leaving an `unaccounted` physical orphan.

The resurrect-reupload fix makes `closeBlob` HEAD the current token when a prior retired entry reaches zero in-degree and condemns the current token if it differs from the retired token, matching `CaIncarnationCore`'s `GRetire` behavior.

An abandoned precommit manifest could remain permanently protected when `CasOrphanManifestSweep` saw a `Precommit` binding with no removal event; a content-static shard parked by token-diff `Skip` prevented `reclaimAbandonedPrecommit` from running again.

To reclaim abandoned precommits on parked shards, `Gc::computeDiscoverDecisions` force-reads a token-stable shard when its sealed minimal live precommit is dead according to the mount watermark, allowing `reclaimAbandonedPrecommit` to emit the owner removal.

`system.content_addressed_log` should expose manifest lifecycle events per object: `manifest_put` for body writes, `precommit_removed` for writer-side abandonment, and a distinct `precommit_reclaim` for GC-side reclaim; dead `ManifestExpand`, `ManifestRetire`, and `ManifestStrip` enum entries were removed.

`clickhouse-disks cas-inspect <key>` is a read-only CLI that decodes recognized CA layouts using `decodeRootShard`, `decodePartManifest`, `decodeMountLease`, `decodeGcState`, `decodeFoldSeal`, `decodeRetiredSet`, and `CasEnvelope` for `blobs/`; unknown keys fail with `BAD_ARGUMENTS` rather than guessing.

Before its fix, `Build::promote` could overwrite an existing committed `refs[R]` without emitting a removal for the old binding, leaving two committed owner bindings for `R` and permanently pinning the old manifest and uniquely-owned blobs.

The promote-over-committed fix fails closed with `ABORTED` when `refs[final_ref_name]` names a different committed manifest, while `ContentAddressedTransaction::republishRef` is idempotent for a destination with the same path-sorted entries and throws `ABORTED` for different content.

`Build::abandon` must call `retireBuildSeq` only after the precommit-removal `mutateShard`, so the build becomes watermark-dead only after its removal is durable; this ordering mirrors `Build::promote`.

An inline-only CA part could reach `publishStaging` with nonempty staged entries and `st.build == nullptr`, causing a `LOGICAL_ERROR`; the inline write path now calls `buildFor(route, st)` so an all-inline part has a `Build`.

The tokenless DETACH/freeze adopt path can race GC condemnation because `copyForwardFromCondemned` runs once before the CAS closure; the proposed fix is a bounded copy-forward and re-HEAD loop outside the closure, analogous to tokened resurrection.

The writer-GC simplification review rejected both unchanged-round promote HEAD skipping and per-commit pinned-round acknowledgements as unnecessary variants after adopting the `EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE` design; the durable precommit edge plus two-phase delete recheck remains the load-bearing safety mechanism.

The `EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE` writer order is body, `precommitAdd`, `putBlob`, then `promote`; it makes the precommit closure edge durable before blob adoption and is relied on by the two-phase GC deletion recheck.

A GC removal-fold wedge can clamp a shard forever when `CasOrphanManifestSweep` deletes a promoted manifest body after `dropRef` but before the committed-removal `-1` is sealed; the fold then cannot read the body to compute edge deltas and pool-wide graduation stops.

The GC-wedge fix protects pending removals of every owner kind: in `activeManifestKeys`, any removal with `transition_version > sealedFoldCursor` keeps its `old_binding` manifest body active until the removal `-1` is sealed; the sweep also emits a manifest-delete audit event.

A custom CAS disk created through the inline `disk(...)` AST function can remain cached in `Context` after its last table is dropped, leaving `ContentAddressedGC` and `MountLeaseKeeper` threads running against deleted backing storage; the lease thread can then raise a process-aborting `LOGICAL_ERROR`.

Custom CAS disk lifecycle still needs a teardown hook or pool reference counting that stops `ContentAddressedGC` and `MountLeaseKeeper` when the last table reference is dropped; absent-backend handling is only defense in depth.

`CasJsonWriter` reduced representative `BM_EncodeRefLogTxn` latency from 753 ns to 333 ns by bulk-appending one record at a time, but the proposed <=3x memcpy-floor gate was not met because the validating encoder remained about 10.8x above the 30.7 ns raw-copy floor.

Raw appending of canonical ref names was rejected because `checkCanonicalRefName` does not reject quotes, control bytes, or U+2028/U+2029; only the fixed vocabulary words `owner` and `tombstone` were proven safe for raw append.

Before the incremental budget fix, `admits()` rebuilt and encoded the full ref table for each state-growing operation, scaling as O(N log N) with live ref count N; `BM_Admits` ranged from 48.8 microseconds at N=100 to 55,976 microseconds at N=100,000.

The incremental `admits()` fix maintains byte-exact body-size counters in `RefTableState` through `applyOpInPlace`, making a K-operation flush O(K) instead of O(K×N); measurements became approximately 1.8–1.9 microseconds across N=100 through N=100,000.

A transient S3 `NETWORK_ERROR` during CAS ref-table startup recovery can leave an `AsyncLoader` job permanently `FAILED`; ClickHouse `AsyncLoader` has no retry or requeue path for a failed table job, so the table remains unavailable until restart or an explicit new load job.

A lazy CAS table reattached as a `StorageTableProxy` can block its first-access build in the ref-namespace LIST inside `CasRefLedger::ensureRefTableRecovered` for the entire object-store outage; the table self-heals after the store returns because the proxy job remains `OK` rather than entering a terminal `AsyncLoader` failure.

A measured 500-partition wide INSERT was 170.6 seconds on CA versus 22.4 seconds on standard S3, despite fewer PUTs; the CA cost was dominated by serial per-part ref commits, serial per-blob uploads, manifest GET validation, and speculative `deduplication_head_first_min_bytes = 1 MiB` HEADs.
The CA upload path uses `deduplication_head_first_min_bytes` with a default of 1 MiB, causing a HEAD-before-PUT for large blobs; on fresh data the measured 498/498 HEADs missed and avoided zero PUTs.

S42 is intended to fault allocations through the per-query `memory_tracker_fault_probability` setting and thread creation through `cannot_allocate_thread_fault_injection_probability`, then verify that durable CAS state, replicas, fsck, and post-restart views remain consistent even when queries fail.

The S42 allocation-fault oracle must require a nonzero injected-failure count or report `inconclusive`; a generic nonzero `MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` count does not prove that a post-durable-PUT in-memory-apply window was exercised.

All scenario GC verdicts became vacuous when `framework/observe.gc_log_rows` queried the removed `min_ack` column, caught `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`, and returned an empty row set; `assert_gc_no_failed` then passed on empty input.

Harness observation helpers must distinguish a legitimately empty table or not-yet-flushed log from a failed observation; schema/query errors must surface instead of becoming empty results, and row-set assertions need explicit non-vacuity guards.

The S12 ten-replica harness uses `docker-compose-10replicas.yml`, `Cluster(node_count=10)`, and one command to validate 10-replica byte-identical convergence, CA deduplication, and `fsck dangling=0/unreachable=0`.

A `shadow/<bk>` directory on CA must be tombstone-aware: `existsDirectory` must enumerate namespaces with `listNamespaces` and consult tombstone-aware `listRefs`, because raw LIST counts tombstoned objects that have not yet been garbage-collected.

The fsck phantom-dangling fix re-resolves every referencing ref at both HEAD-absent branches; a missing blob is `dangling` only if a current ref still names it, not when the ref was legitimately re-published or dropped after the initial walk.

A 4-hour chaos soak can become blind when detail-less fsck exceeds its 180-second bound at about 2.14 million objects; long-run validation also needs a TTL-band oracle that does not hard-fail during an active fault window and a pool-size or compaction limit.
The CAS event log's manifest identity must be namespace-qualified because an unqualified `manifest_ref_instance` such as `1:308:1` can collide across tables and mislead incident forensics.

The consolidation coverage matrix is the mandatory deletion gate: a source document may not be deleted unless the matrix maps its durable invariants, decisions, rejected paths, and load-bearing technical details to consolidated targets; ephemeral play-by-play is intentionally excluded.

The TLA+ model sources, active D1 work, the consolidation design and plan, current D2 triage, the runfile streaming backlog, and the entire new `cas/` folder are explicitly retained rather than treated as deletion candidates.

The CAS path boundary uses an `@cas@` archive suffix on the table directory, never as a standalone segment; a node is immutable exactly when it is content-addressed, and `@cas@` marks the content-addressed/verbatim boundary.

CA path mirroring distinguishes Atomic `store/<u3>/<uuid>@cas@` namespaces from non-Atomic `data/<db>/<tbl>@cas@` namespaces, and numeric-tailed loose files without an `@cas@` ancestor are opaque ordinary files rather than shards.

CA namespaces must not nest because GC enumerates by prefix LIST; the two verbatim-file locations are loose files under `roots/<server>/<path>` and files under `@cas@/_files/`, while the `_disk` magic namespace was eliminated.

`clickhouse-disks` exposes the logical `@cas@`-stripped view, whereas raw S3 listing exposes the physical archive; recursively removing a raw subtree is destructive maintenance and is not equivalent to `dropNamespace`.
The CaIncarnationCore publish gate must consult durable deleted-token history `deadTok[h]`, not only the in-flight `retired` set.

Any action that stops a token being current, including delete-land, `WResurrect`, and `WOverwrite`, must push the displaced token into `deadTok[h]`; publish must revalidate the dependency's current physical state rather than only the originally observed token.
A tree ref may be published only when all direct children are present and non-condemned at publish time, enforcing bottom-up `TreeDepsOK` construction.
GC condemnation is fail-closed: a candidate absent at condemn time, including a HEAD 404, is skipped and no token is fabricated.

A missing or invalid committed/promoted new-binding manifest body clamps the affected GC shard with `classification = 4`; precommit bindings are non-activating, old-binding removals use fold-sealed edges, and GC never reads a deleted manifest body.

The GC publish-order invariant requires the retired-list runs for round K to be durable before the single `gc/state` CAS publishes `round := K` and `retired_refs`; refs and round are published together so round K always has a loadable retired list K.
SQL DROP PART or DROP PARTITION is represented by a covering tombstone ref in the CAS model, distinct from the D1 shard-object tombstone.
FREEZE must materialize real bytes into `shadow/` rather than create reference-only snapshots; `shadow/` is a GC reachability root and UNFREEZE releases its refs.
A patch-part manifest is a first-class reachability root that keeps both its delta blobs and the referenced base blobs alive transitively.

Cross-replica manifest divergence is benign for correctness because single-producer publication is only an optimization; commit-time `checkEqual` is tolerant, and this rationale governs the `manifest_hash` TODO.
A stateless or ref-less reader is protected from GC with an ephemeral reader pin and a lost-replica timeout; the per-server-owned-namespace model narrows but does not eliminate the race window.

Incarnation identity is stored in the object body rather than provider metadata because metadata is write-once and requires copy operations, has an 8 KiB cap, and S3 ETags identify content rather than metadata.
`ObjectStorageBackend::get` maps NoSuchKey/HTTP 404 to `std::nullopt`, allowing a legitimate live read in a HEAD-to-GET deletion window to surface cleanly instead of exposing raw Code 499.
Resident-snapshot incremental GC uses `gc_checkpoint_records=4096` and `gc_checkpoint_rounds=64`; trimming is allowed only at or below the durable cursor, not merely the resident cursor.
`shard_decode_cache_ttl_ms` defaults to 200, and absence is never TTL-cached.
A projection is represented by nested `<proj>.proj/<file>` keys inside the parent part's single `PartManifest`; nested sub-manifests and a separate `projections/` ref namespace were rejected.
Committed projection discovery requires `existsDirectory` and `listDirectory` projection-subdirectory branches that collapse `<proj>.proj/*` to one `<proj>.proj` entry when listing the parent part.

Same-pool fetch-by-relink detection must use a stable minted `pool_uuid` stored in `_pool_meta`, not endpoint-and-prefix string matching, because aliases can cause false negatives and shared proxies can cause false positives that relink to absent blobs.

A fresh FETCH landing commits a `detached` ref by folding the transaction's `recorded` blobs into the shared detached ref and rekeys `detached/tmp-fetch_<part>` to `detached/<part>` with `rekeyDetachedPartDir`.
FREEZE uses one ref per frozen part rather than a shared container to avoid shared-`detached` read-modify-write and B66a torn-read hazards under concurrent freeze.

The transactional MVCC layer uses `IMetadataStorage::supportsTransactionalMutableFiles` separately from `supportWritingWithAppend`; CA must not report `supportWritingWithAppend = true` because that would defeat the dedup-log no-append fallback and disarm the append guard.

When a transaction has `recorded` empty, `recorded_mutable` nonempty, and an existing ref, `commit` must update only the mutable sidecar in place while preserving the existing `part_id`, manifest, and ref; with no ref it must throw rather than publish a standalone empty sidecar.

`replaceFile` routes a mutable-file destination to `recorded_mutable`, and the temporary name must itself satisfy `isMutablePerPartFile` as `<mutable>.tmp`; otherwise standalone autocommit can republish a one-file manifest and clobber the part.

On CA, an uncommitted INSERT publishes a ref whose blobs remain GC-reachable but is governed-invisible through `txn_version.txt`; ROLLBACK removes the ref and makes the blobs GC-eligible, while `getLastModified` on a ref-less in-flight part must use the in-flight overlay.

A multi-part disk transaction uses a per-part `std::map<{table_uuid, part_name}, PartStaging>` and can span a deferred `tmp_merge_X → X` rename plus `txn_version.txt` rewrites for covered source parts; CA publishes parts one at a time, with MVCC visibility providing logical atomicity and GC reclaiming crash-orphaned refs.

The consolidation's second-pass audit found that mapping multi-part disk transactions to `03 §phase-upload (multipart)` and transaction machinery to `03 §mutable-vs-immutable` were incorrect; both belong in `03 §transactions-mvcc`.

The first coverage pass treated the transactional-commit machinery as covered, but the second-pass audit identified it as a significant load-bearing gap along with projection representation, committed projection listing, `pool_uuid` relink identity, fresh-fetch detached landing, and the per-part freeze rationale; all were later filled additively.

The read-path gap-fill recovered B59 projection readback, its `tryGetInFlight*` overlay, directory-granularity overlay rules, and B115 `ReadBufferFromFileView` position rebasing into `09-read-protocol.md`; B115 passed 36/36 gtests after the fix versus 14/36 before it.

The coverage audit considers the backup/restore source a thin RESTORE bug-fix specification rather than architecture: `BACKUP` read-side works, while `RESTORE` must materialize each part through one whole-part commit rather than per-file autocommit.
The intermediate grace-based GC designs were intentionally superseded by the incarnation, pin, lease, and fence model; this is treated as intended design history rather than lost durable content.
The CAS drop-in goal is `metadata_type = content_addressed` with no DDL or engine change; acceptance work includes the B31 gate, removal of tags, and no-leftovers GC.
Whole-part partition cloning for ATTACH, REPLACE, and MOVE PARTITION on the same disk uses one ref to the source `part_id` and performs zero byte copying.

The cleanup simplification removed vestigial `trees/` and `ObjectKind::Tree`, the `_disk` namespace, the registry, and `Placement::Pack`, and unified configuration keys; the R1–R14 refactor task list is intentionally dropped as process history.

The coverage matrix records that all second-pass gaps were filled additively in the consolidated docs, while the transactions-design iterative tail was intentionally excluded because it was a testing observation rather than a documented invariant.
